To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) ranking is a fundamental property that is missing from RDBMS, (2) ranking queries can be supported by extending relational algebra with rank-relational operators, and (3) ranking query optimization is possible by enumerating rank-relational plans and estimating the cardinality of new operators.

(1) the ranking relationship can be captured in relational model as a new logical property of data (2) a pipelined execution model of ranking queries is possible, (3) a new plan space can be defined and explored to optimize ranking queries, and (4) a new estimation model can be developed to estimate cardinality of rank-relational operators.

1) we introduce a new relational algebra that supports ranking queries in RDBMS; 2) we present a novel incremental execution model for top-k queries; 3) we propose a plan space enumeration algorithm that explores the new plan space; 4) we introduce a sampling-based estimation model for ranking queries.
